messages:
maya (CS): Hey team — onboarding for AcmePay hitting strange auth behavior in staging. They see intermittent 401s during SDK init followed by a flood of 429s against our edge. Root cause unclear, customer is blocked. Anyone seen a refresh-race + edge-splay issue?

devon (eng): which SDK? mobile or server-side? can you paste a redacted log snippet and the init headers?

maya (CS): mobile (react-native). Log pattern: 401 for init, client does token exchange, then ~200ms later a bunch of subsequent requests return 429. Sample headers: `Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>`, `x-client-id: acmepay`, `x-edge-id` toggles between edges.

olga (solutions): we've seen this when clients aggressively refresh ephemeral tokens and immediately replay requests. If preflight/auth cache hasn't propagated across edges, you get initial 401 then burst of traffic that trips rate limiting.

dennis (sre): our auth-cache TTL at the edge is 2s for new ephemeral tokens; if they rotate too fast and land on different edge nodes, they can look unauthenticated then flood the origin. Do we have `Retry-After` headers in the 429s?

maya (CS): yes some 429 responses include `Retry-After: 1` and some are plain 429. Here's a short redacted log sequence:
```
[12:03:21] client/init -> POST /v1/init 401 invalid_token
[12:03:22] client/token -> POST /auth/exchange 200 ok
[12:03:22] client/req -> POST /v1/completions 200
[12:03:22] client/req -> POST /v1/completions 429 rate_limited (edge-12)
[12:03:22] client/req -> POST /v1/completions 429 rate_limited (edge-27)
```

devon (eng): couple quick asks: can they enable session affinity / keep-alive to reduce edge hopping? also flip on a small client-side jitter/splay so refreshes don't align. In the SDK config they can set a short leeway and limit concurrent inits. Example config we recommend: 
```
sdk.configure({
  maxInitConcurrency: 2,
  ephemeralTokenLeewayMs: 3000,
  initRetryBaseMs: 150,
  initRetryMultiplier: 1.6
});
```

olga (solutions): also advise the customer to debounce token refresh on background resume. We've seen mobile OSes cause many apps to re-init at once after unlock. A 500–1000ms randomized jitter usually fixes the stampede.

dennis (sre): on our side we can temporarily raise auth-cache TTL to 5s for that deployment and allow slightly higher per-edge burst capacity while they test. I'll open a short-lived rule, but need CS approval to change config.

maya (CS): please do that @dennis, thanks. I'll push the SDK patch suggestion to the client and ask them to test with `maxInitConcurrency: 1` + jitter.

onboard-bot: Created support ticket CS-4821: "AcmePay mobile init handshake -> 401 then 429 storm" assigned to devon, priority P1.

devon (eng): I'll take the ticket. If the customer can attach a HAR or sequence of `x-edge-id` values we can confirm edge-hopping. Also ask them to try rotating a non-ephemeral key once to rule out clock skew.

maya (CS): sent the ask to the customer. Quick follow-up plan: 1) apply SDK config patch with jitter/leeway, 2) we (SRE) bump auth-cache TTL for staging for 30m, 3) customer retests and shares logs. I'll update CS-4821 with results.

olga (solutions): great. if this recurs after changes we'll recommend using a short-lived server-side token exchange (one per device) to reduce client-side refresh frequency.

dennis (sre): patched staging TTL to 5s for `acmepay-staging` for 30m window. monitor dashboards for 10m.

maya (CS): :thumbsup: thanks everyone, will report back once customer tests.
